- When sentiment is strongly bullish (≥0.75) and forecast shows a sharp upward spike, reduce the peak by 5–10% to avoid over-optimism.  
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) and forecast remains flat or rising, lower the forecast 3–5% to reflect risk-off behavior.  
- After a strong price spike (e.g., >10% from prior day), model tends to overshoot — apply a 2–4 day lag correction by reducing forecast by 2–5% per day.  
- When sentiment is mixed (0.33–0.75) and price shows mean reversion, model often overcorrects — dampen forecast by 3–7% for 2–3 days.  
- If forecast is consistently higher than true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a downward bias correction of 1–3% per day, especially if sentiment is neutral or slightly bullish.  
- For 30-day horizon, if true outcome shows a downward trend after a peak, model often fails to recognize it — adjust forecast to align with 10–15 day moving average of true values.
